purpose: Public-safe, machine-readable reconstruction of legal representation, legal-adviser, procurador and expert-witness interfaces across the Sun Park / Aweswell / LPB / Matkator matter. Designed as a backend source for later bilingual website views. Absence from this seed does not mean absence from the evidence base.

method.privateEvidenceBoundary: Do not publish raw mailbox identifiers, private email addresses, privileged correspondence, personal assessments or unredacted source material from private systems.
method.negativeEvidenceRule: Use 'not yet located' or 'no filing evidence located' unless non-existence or non-filing is affirmatively established.
method.handoverRule: A change of lawyer, firm or procurador is a separate event and must be tied to the client and matter affected; do not force parallel representations into one linear chain.
method.expertWitnessRule: Experts and expert witnesses are not legal counsel. Track report receipt, substantive use, procurador transmission and court filing as separate states.
method.publicCharacterisationRule: Describe conduct through dated, verifiable acts and omissions. Private or subjective assessments are not converted into public factual assertions.

documentedActivities: Received and reviewed expert/economic material before the formal May 2020 takeover.

Entered a bilingual engagement accepted on 22 May 2020 providing for direct Aweswell instructions, proposed removal of the Administrador Concursal and assessment of possible claims against the AC and Acosta Matos; Cuatrecasas granted venia on 26 May 2020.
Coordinated directly with expert David Espejo and reviewed swap/insolvency issues.

On 28 May Juan Tomás Parrilla conveyed the AC's request to speak to incoming counsel; after a contemporaneous client warning about off-record intermediation, Daniel took and reported the direct 1 June AC call.

The 1 June call report records proposed peace and possible complaint withdrawal, assurance that Parrilla and the procurator would be paid, praise of Parrilla and IA/CAM positions. This supports an influence-route inference but does not prove unlawful motive or collusion.

On 5 June Daniel reported that CAM's lawyer had asked the AC to arrange contact. The client instructed claims first and no information disclosure; a CAM call was proposed but has not been proved to have occurred.
SLJ later claimed 55 hours of review, calls and drafting. Decree 316/2021 found no procedural filing during the mandate signed by Daniel/SLJ and treated the alleged court filing as unproved.
The documentary record shows a short engagement ending with a resignation announcement on 23 June 2020 before any verified signed procedural filing by Daniel/SLJ.

In the later fee proceeding SLJ stated that Aweswell had supplied 4,458 documents and on 4 December 2020 filed a 179-page inventory extracted from its client database plus selected client material. The filing did not include every underlying file; the LexNET wrapper shows immediate copy-transfer only to Aweswell's procurator.
knowledgeStateAtEnd: Possessed multiple David Espejo reports/notes and later swap-analysis material.

SLJ later described its database as containing a 4,458-document Aweswell client file and filed the full 179-page inventory in the fee proceeding.
clientPositionAndLimits: Gil/Patricia say Daniel was expressly instructed before engagement not to speak to the AC or Acosta Matos before protective claims were filed. The exact pre-contract wording has not been located, but contemporaneous 28 May and 5 June emails corroborate the protective sequencing, anti-intermediation and no-information substance.

Gil/Patricia characterise the rapid change in Daniel's tone and position as hostile and infer that the AC sought to instrumentalise Parrilla's departure to influence incoming counsel. The 28 May-5 June sequence supports investigation of that inference, not publication of unlawful intent, collusion or exit causation as proved fact.

The client describes SLJ's retention/use of the client data room as theft. No adjudication or source located proves theft; the controlled questions are authority to retain, litigation necessity, confidentiality, proportionality and actual access or prejudice.
